datasets.title: Bangladesh - Cox's Bazar District - Refugee Camp WASH Infrastructure Coding 2019
datasets.description: In early 2019, UNICEF and the Cox's Bazar WASH sector identified a need to comprehensively map key WASH infrastructure using physical unique identifier (UUID) tags, in order to produce a database containing information about each piece of infrastructure across the camps. The objectives of this effort were to facilitate accurate, consistent spatial identification of unique infrastructure by all interested actors, to provide a baseline 'snapshot' of WASH infrastructure functionality at the time of coding, and to establish a common dataset to be used by all partners. The core infrastructure being covered by this exercise includes tubewells, latrines, and bathing facilities.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cox-s-bazar-district-refugee-camp-wash-infrastructure-coding-2019]

lineage.description: WASH infrastructure across Cox's Bazar refugee camps was comprehensively mapped in 2019 through a census-based approach using physical unique identifier (UUID) tags. Data collection involved UNICEF and Cox's Bazar WASH sector partners documenting tubewell and sanitation infrastructure with spatial coordinates (KML format) and functionality assessments. The resulting database serves as a baseline inventory for infrastructure management and partner coordination.

resources.title: KML for partner use (per camp).zip
resources.description: This zip folder contains KML files with the tubewells and their barcodes per camp. These KML files can be loaded into navigation software such as Google Maps or MAPS.ME on tablets and smartphones and used to navigate to specific tubewells in the field. See guidance note on how to upload these files to your smartphone.

resources.title: SOP_updating_the_database_tubewell_decommissioning.docx
resources.description: In order for the Tubewell Coding database to stay up to date and relevant, it requires frequent updating in case tubewells are decommissioned. This Standard Operational Procedures describes the process of how the Tubewell Coding database will be updated when facilities are being decommissioned.
